```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
library(CEClust)
```

`CECdiagram` is the common entry point in version 0.4.0.9000. It combines
the adaptive engine from CEClust 0.3.0.9010 and the experimental bands
engine from CEClustBands 0.1.0.9001. Their searches and diagnostics remain
separate. The method selector does not make their outputs interchangeable.

```{r usage, eval=FALSE}
grid <- CECdiagram(X, method="adaptive", L=20, B=20, workers=4,
                   seed=1, directory="adaptive_run")
bands <- CECdiagram(X, method="bands", L=20, B=20, workers=4,
                    seed=1, directory="bands_run")
```

## Adaptive grid

The default method uses CEM, propagation and subdivision. The common entry
point computes `Cmin` from the peak of the Gaussian fitted to the complete
sample, with covariance divided by n. The ten initial C centres are
`2^(1:10) * Cmin`. Left extension is disabled. Extension to the right and
along lambda, and refinement, remain available. Cell edges retain the
engine's half-step convention. This Cmin is an exploration reference,
not a universal saturation guarantee.

```{r initialization}
X <- matrix(c(-3,-2,-1,1,2,3), ncol=1)
CECinitialGrid(X)
```

A singular full-sample covariance produces an explicit error. Supply
`C_grid` explicitly or remove redundant variables. No hidden regularization
is introduced. `lambda_grid` can also be supplied explicitly.

```{r adaptive-control, eval=FALSE}
control <- CECdiagramControl("adaptive",
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=20, Ninit=5),
  adaptive_control=list(extend_left=FALSE, max_cells=12000))
grid <- CECdiagram(X, "adaptive", control=control, directory="grid_2")
CECsummariseGrid(grid)
CECplotGrid(grid)
```

Historical direct calls to `CECfitBoundGrid` retain their old defaults.
The EM-bank variant remains available through
`control=list(optimization="em_bank")`.

## Candidate bands

The common entry point uses the last agreed budget: pilot orders 1:20,
5 starts per order, 2 extra starts, 10 anchors, enriched order limit 40,
11 initial and at most 41 C columns, 2 refinement rounds, 2 projection
rounds and 200 projection queries. The default retention thresholds are
algorithmic stability above 0.85, RSI above 0.95 and zero saturation.

```{r bands-control, eval=FALSE}
control <- CECdiagramControl("bands", max_anchors=10, extra_starts=2)
bands <- CECdiagram(X, "bands", control=control, directory="bands_2")
bands_partitions(bands)
bands_plot(bands)
bands_validate(bands)
```

`penalty="bic"` is available for either method. `bands_cleanup` remains
a separate optional call. It screens retained partitions by subdivision
and CEM, without inserting replacement partitions or recomputing RSI.
This integration does not resolve the known exploration limitations of
the bands engine. Direct `cec_bands` and `bands_control` calls retain
their historical, larger default budgets.

## Saving and resuming

Use one directory per run. Keep the full directory: bands results refer
to allocation files there. `diagram.rds` stores the returned result.
Use `resume=TRUE` with the same data and parameters to resume a run.
Checkpoints from the separate historical packages are not reused by
the unified runtime.
